title: New Capenna Commander: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Some crime scenes' secrets can only be discerned from an angel's-eye view.
"Guilty as charged!"
The roar of applause drowned out the melee raging in the lobby.
Obscura spies rarely stay locked up long enough to make it to trial.
One way or another, everyone gets paid what they're owed.
Few think to look past a familiar face and a friendly smile.
"Just one aether tiger? What do I look like, a peasant?"
Beware the fine print.
He's pretty sure he can't get charged with murder if he calls it "organic demolition."
"Your friends stayed quiet, and look what happened to them. You feeling a little more talkative yet?"
As the Adversary's influence grew, the conflicts between families escalated.
"Only a fool believes they have nothing left to learn."
In New Capenna, it's survival of the richest.
The profits from that night barely paid for the damages.
Sometimes the trash throws you out.
All the money in the world won't buy back a pulse.
"So many fools think throwing something away is the same as disposing of it."
Partners in love, partners in life, and partners in crime.
"That performance was truly the pits." —Jetmir
His enthusiastic curiosity puts even the most fearsome of beasts at ease.
Late payment shall be extracted however they see fit.
Every work of art is a hit.
"I teach the cubs how to kill the two-legs quickly, and why it's best for the pride."
When the alarm crystals flash, Drannith's finest answer the call.
The best techniques outlive their creators.
"They had it coming." —Squire Imalia, savior of Thiswick
The best presents are impossible to regift.
In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.
"Rally to my light, and together we will drive out this darkness!"
Their war forgotten, the nations of Bant stood united in the face of a common threat.
The Orzhov care not for repentance, only repayment.
A blazing sun that never sets.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."
Their lust for battle was so great that they didn't care their enemies wore their own faces.
"They'll never see me coming."
"The specimen seems to be broken."
"From a sea of infinite possibilities, our choices create the future." —Mu Yanling
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."
It took the banning of temporal manipulation at Tolaria West to teach its students the value of time.
Unable to touch items of value, he goes forth to steal secrets instead.
Tomorrow belongs to those who prepare for it today.
Carefully following the thaumatic compass Bolas had given her, Vraska blundered straight into the River Heralds' trap.
Escapes should always be daring.
After Talrand conquered the depths of Shandalar, his ambitions drove him skyward, joined by servants whose drive and curiosity equaled his own.
Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.
Their bond grew over time, as did the height of their jumps.
Zndrsplt retired from officiating when she teamed up with Okaun, but she still knows the penalties better than anyone else.
"May you wake to find you were only ever a dream." —Mephidross curse
Sometimes death comes knocking. Sometimes it tears down the walls.
"Death is merely another foe the Mardu will overcome."
"Keeping order is a task too important to relinquish in death." —Abrado, Custodi priest
"Silumgar's mind is a dark labyrinth, full of grim secrets and subtle traps." —Siara, the Dragon's Mouth
"Lord Bolas has shown me how each miserable little life holds untold resources."
"I will not live as a slave. If you would be free, then fight alongside me."
"Did you have a nice nap?" —Liliana Vess
"On vile wings and bloody wind, the swarm will rise." —Skyclave inscription
When killing five just isn't enough.
As the Eldrazi spread, no secret that could give Zendikar's defenders an advantage was considered too dangerous to seek.
"Die. But die knowing that your pathetic life will yield a great bounty for me." —Zul Ashur, lich lord
"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything." —Thalia, Knight-Cathar
"We train for the improbable, like lightning striking the same place twice, or striking everywhere at once." —Nundari, Sea Gate militia captain
"Your eyes aren't playing tricks on you. I am."
The storm rages and the earth breaks.
Warning to those who scale the cliffs without paying tribute: It's a long way down.
"Fate is not as fixed as you might think."
"You gotta be pretty smart to live long as me, but not being able to die helps."
Something roams the killing places, sniffing the guilt of the slayers, stalking them on iron paws.
"Listen to the roar! Feel the thunder! The Immersturm shouts its approval with every bolt of lightning!"
Her webs, spun from her own hair, reach from Nyx to the mortal world and even into the Underworld.
The ground erupted in time with the hedron's thrum, a dirge of the last days.
"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them." ―Euphemia, Nexus watcher
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
"Mana lurks in all things, even in the depths of one's own heart."
"To care for yourself, cultivate the world. To care for the world, cultivate yourself."
The essence of nature is change.
An explorer's reward is a view of tomorrow's possibilities.
"How truly vast this city must be, that I have traveled so far and seen so much, yet never once found the place where the buildings fail."
Its blood is life. Its body is growth.
"To a creature like that, we must seem like, well, bugs." —Dars Gostok, Firefist captain
"Animals commune with their environment without the need for language. Theirs is a fundamental connection that surpasses flimsy words." —Vivien Reid
"An indrik's howl has destructive power much subtler than that of its crushing foot. The sound is mundane, but inaudible vibrations scatter and sunder magical contrivances." —Simic research notes
"The land grows only where the kami will it." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
"I am rooted in the life of all that thrives around me. You cannot move me."
At the instant of death, the mystery of life.
"Our enemy is nothing less than the end of all life. We shall not want for allies." —*The War Diaries*
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
"Aether is the soul of Kaladesh, and all souls should be free."
"Control the Great Conduit? You might as well try to divert a river with your hands."
There were no tombstones in orochi territory. Slain warriors were buried with a tree sapling, so they would become a part of the forest after death.
Cantankerous and territorial, sandwurms claim even the skies above their dunes.
In nature, not a single bone or scrap of flesh goes to waste.
"Survival rule 782: There are *always* more scute bugs." —Zurdi, goblin shortcutter
First, whispers of ancient days. Then, visions of things to come.
Many an ancient treasure has been reduced to jagged caltrops by its snapping jaws.
The Temur see themselves as a pack, their bonds more primal than the Abzan's.
"Always carry two spears." —Mokgar, Kalonian hunter
"Odd. I didn't see any lightning . . . ." —Herreth, poacher, last words
The wisdom of the past is written on the bones of ancients.
"Mana grows and changes like the roots of a plant. Like a plant, it must be nurtured." —Nissa Revane
"Living scarecrows make a mockery of the natural order. Dead ones make fine hats."
Every branch a crossroads, every vine a swift steed.
"The Great River will not be tamed."
"Rankle's pranks are child's play. My games will topple kingdoms."
"There's nothing technology can build that nature can't eventually reclaim." —Vivien Reid
"Nature has a way of adapting to and overcoming any force that seeks its end." —Vivien Reid
"If the skies are our only refuge, I will see all of us take wing."
Bant is a world where death and chaos hold no sway.
"It's easy to get taken in by the spectacle, to enjoy a bit of naughty amusement. But make no mistake: the Cult of Rakdos is a danger." —Tajic
It hears and answers every orison across Shadowmoor.
"Within the song of Mat'Selesnya, one becomes all." —Heruj, Selesnya hierophant
"All who set foot in Paliano are pawns in someone's play for power." —Marchesa, the Black Rose
He can stir the gentlest spirit to wild ferocity.
When asked how much power is required, Izzet mages always answer "more."
The murk of the Wanderbrine concealed unseemly rituals designed to bring out the worst in merrowkind.
Wounded soldiers looked up, grateful for her appearance. But she passed over them, her eyes firmly on their foe.
"Loss has no meaning here. You cannot take from those who have nothing."
Each of his twenty-two braids is bound with bone and leather from a foe.
"Our forces number more than the leaves of Vitu-Ghazi. Do not provoke us."
"From this day forward, we confront this world together, lifting each other up."
"The Lowlands refuse to suffer at the whims of the High City."
All suns must set.
As the Simic released more of their krasis experiments, they required new habitats, always at the expense of the locals.
"I came seeking a challenge. All I found was you." —Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
"I used to hurl rocks and eat scraps of meat burned over a fire. Look at what I've become and tell me Simic does not hold infinite possibility."
Not all who remember Urza do so with fondness.
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.
The weapon wields the hand that holds it.
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
"Arise, great one, and cleanse the world of our enemies!"
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
"Inspiration is found by looking outward." —Oviya Pashiri, sage lifecrafter
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
The sigil holds different meanings depending on its form and presentation. While some wear it as a sign of status, others wear it as a sign of debt.
Never content, vedalken artificers continually tinker with their creations.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
Its tines cannot be rung by mere physical force. Only magic of great power can start its eldritch resonance.
"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat . . . if you're prepared." —Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords
Druids hold certain plants to be sacred and use their leaves and wood as a spellcasting focus.
"We must rely on our own knowledge, not on the dogma of the seekers or the mutterings of the sphinxes." —Tullus of Palandius
Bant's hearts are as pure as its air and as bright as its skies.
The continent of Murasa lies beneath a blanket of dense vegetation, its enormous branches tangled so thickly that some inhabitants never see the ground.
Travelers bathe in the falls to wash away curses from the pucas who lurk nearby.
Without Ardenvale's loyalty, the realm would greedily devour itself.
Without Embereth's courage, the realm would falter and fall.
On the volcanic continent of Akoum, bizarre vegetation clusters around gas vents, and jagged mountain peaks rise high into the air.
"Approach my tower on bended knee or depart from it as ash upon the wind." —Gadwick, the Wizened
"They say the ruins of Sedraxis were once a shining capital in Vithia. Now it is a blight, a place to be avoided by the living." —Olcot, Rider of Joffik
Murky Otarian tides hide the forgotten treacheries of the Phyrexian war.
Esper is an expansive canvas painted by precise, controlling hands.
"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them." —Pulan, Bant orchardist
"Do not linger in such places, child. There the gwyllions dance. If they find you, you will join in their revels for eternity." —Talara, elvish safewright
At full moon, the river seeps over its banks and crawls through the woods like a blanket of serpents.
"The protective wards of the church have weakened, and no one can tell us why. It's time to look to our own defenses." —Gregel, militia leader
There is no height above Grixis that is free from the stench of death.
The sky is the dragon's throne, the seat from which it issues its fiery decrees.
On Naya, ambition and treachery are scarce, hunted nearly to extinction by the awe owed to terrestrial gods.
"I can't protect everyone here. But those I can, I will." —Karn
When a werewolf changes for the first time, that first howl is said to echo through the wilds till moonset.
Plant life in the valley changes for the worse as runoff from dwarven forges contaminates the water.
Between the thunderous footfalls of Naya's behemoths lie moments of perfect quiet.
Dappled coats become armored hides. Soft jaws become razor tusks. Nestling play becomes the fight for survival.
The continent of Ondu is a vast plateau crisscrossed by deep trenches and meandering rivers.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
Hobs bury their kin far from home. They believe the dry, open ground keeps hags from stealing the bones and gwyllions from stealing the spirits.
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
Gnolls make offerings to sinister forces in the shadow-drenched chasms.
Legend says a mighty angel appears to pilgrims in need who reach this lofty height.
The continent of Guul Draz is a geothermal swampland reeking of heat and decay.
The ancient magic of sun elves keeps these lands in an eternal summer.
On the continent of Tazeem, rushing waters plunge through narrow canyons into mist-cloaked lakes.
"When gods become apathetic, the people will worship anyone who answers their pleas." —Kiora
As eons passed, the rock wore away, revealing the rich colors at the mountain's heart.
Far from human eyes, birds flit between vivid blossoms in a hidden paradise.
Wildflowers here bloom not with the season but with the ebb and flow of magic.
All the wonders of the natural world in one breathtaking microcosm.
Beauty appears in strange places for those with eyes to see it.
As their roots soaked in a weak tea of bogwater and decay, the trees absorbed the essence of death into their living tissue.
